domainRelevance: Park-Ohio is a mid-market industrial distributor and supplier of components, assemblies, and fluid-power systems to automotive OEMs, aerospace primes, and industrial end-users. The company operates three reportable segments—Automotive, Fluid Power, and Engineered Products—with ~$2.0B in annual revenue and a footprint across North America and Europe. Its role is critical in the supply-chain bridge between commodity material suppliers and final-assembly manufacturers, particularly in cyclical sectors (automotive, aerospace) where inventory management and just-in-time delivery are competitive moats.
portalRelevance: Park-Ohio is a peer-tier industrial distributor whose financial health and operational trajectory serve as a leading indicator for manufacturing-sector demand, capital-equipment spending, and supply-chain stress. Its leverage profile (3.2x debt-to-EBITDA) and exposure to automotive cyclicality make it a barometer for credit-market tightening and recession risk. For equity and credit portfolios, PKOH's quarterly earnings and segment mix shifts signal shifts in aerospace recovery, EV adoption rates, and industrial-capex confidence.

notes.cohortStatus: Peer-tier industrial distributor; comparable to Applied Industrial Technologies (AIT), ScanSource (SCSC), and Anixter (now Anixter International)

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly segment revenue and gross-margin prints (Automotive, Fluid Power, Engineered Products) disclosed in 10-Q filings

Aerospace & defense backlog trends from prime-contractor guidance (Boeing, Lockheed, Raytheon) affecting Engineered Products demand

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (p6 = stable mature distribution; p7 = margin compression / competitive intensity) based on gross-margin trajectory and debt-service coverage
Free-cash-flow runway: current 6-quarter estimate assumes flat EBITDA and $50M annual capex
Leverage cycle: debt-to-EBITDA trending toward 3.0x target; refinancing window Q2 2025 for $300M term loan maturity
Segment mix shift: Engineered Products (aerospace) growing 8–12% CAGR; Automotive flat to declining as OEM production normalizes

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: P6→P7 transition risk if automotive OEM production falls >15% YoY; historical precedent 2008–2009 and 2020 COVID shock
Margin compression signature: gross margin at 18.2% (Q3 2024) vs. 19.1% (Q3 2023); SG&A leverage insufficient to offset
Refinancing stress: $892M debt with 4.8% blended rate; 50 bps rate rise = $4.5M annual interest cost; covenant headroom 1.2x on leverage ratio
Competitive intensity: AIT and ScanSource gaining share in fluid-power and IT-distribution segments; PKOH's niche (automotive + aerospace) narrowing

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: SEC compliance: quarterly 10-Q and annual 10-K filings; Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302/906 certifications; no current SEC investigations or enforcement actions
Debt covenant management: maintain leverage ratio <3.5x and interest-coverage ratio >2.5x; quarterly testing with lender syndicate
Antitrust exposure:; automotive supplier consolidation under FTC scrutiny
Environmental / supply-chain: ITAR compliance for aerospace segment; conflict minerals disclosure under SEC Rule 13p-1

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Debt reduction thesis: target $50M annual debt paydown via free-cash-flow generation; refinance $300M term loan in Q2 2025 at lower rate if market permits
M&A optionality: acquire sub-scale fluid-power or aerospace-component distributors to consolidate fragmented market; target deal size $100–300M
Dividend policy: maintain $0.10/share quarterly dividend (2.1% yield); suspend if leverage exceeds 3.5x or FCF turns negative
Portfolio hedge: long aerospace exposure (F-35, 787 production ramps); short automotive cyclical via sector ETF if OEM guidance deteriorates

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: compare actual segment revenue vs. guidance; gross-margin beat/miss vs. commodity-price expectations
Stock-price reaction: PKOH typically trades 0.8–1.2x book value; price >$50 signals investor confidence in aerospace recovery; <$35 signals distress
Debt-market signals: CDS spread on PKOH 5-year senior unsecured debt; if >400 bps, refinancing risk elevated
Customer concentration: monitor top-10 customer revenue % (currently ~35% of total); loss of major OEM customer (e.g., Ford, GM) triggers 8-K disclosure

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Kernel reweighting: increase aerospace-segment sensitivity if F-35 production accelerates beyond current 156 aircraft/year baseline
Margin model update: incorporate supply-chain normalization impact on gross margin; historical 50 bps swing per 5% inventory reduction
Leverage sensitivity: recalibrate debt-service coverage model if interest rates rise >100 bps; stress-test at 5.5% blended cost of debt
Competitive positioning: monitor AIT and ScanSource quarterly earnings for market-share shifts; adjust PKOH valuation multiple if peer multiples compress

suppliers.name: Eaton Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Eaton is a primary supplier of hydraulic and pneumatic components to PKOH's Fluid Power segment. PKOH distributes Eaton's industrial-grade fluid-power systems to OEM and aftermarket customers across North America. Eaton represents approximately 8–12% of PKOH's Fluid Power segment revenue (estimated $80–120M annually). The relationship includes exclusive distribution agreements in select geographies and co-marketing programs for aerospace-grade components. Disclosed in PKOH 10-K Item 1A supplier concentration risk factors.

suppliers.name: Parker Hannifin Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Parker Hannifin supplies motion-control and fluid-power systems to PKOH's Fluid Power and Engineered Products segments. PKOH is an authorized distributor for Parker's industrial and aerospace product lines, with estimated annual purchases of $60–90M. Parker's aerospace-qualified components (seals, actuators, hoses) are critical to PKOH's F-35 and commercial-aircraft supply-chain participation. Relationship includes technical training programs and joint customer-support initiatives. Disclosed in PKOH 10-K Item 1 business description.

Competitive intensity in aerospace and automotive segments remains moderate due to specialized certification requirements.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: The SEC oversees PKOH's public-company disclosures, including quarterly 10-Q filings, annual 10-K filings, and current 8-K event reports. regulators.name: U.S. Department of Defense (Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency)
regulators.relationshipNote: The DoD's Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversees PKOH's facility security clearance (FSC) and compliance with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) for aerospace and defense contracts. PKOH's Engineered Products segment requires ITAR compliance for F-35 and commercial-aircraft component manufacturing and distribution. PKOH maintains a Secret-level FSC for its manufacturing and distribution facilities. DCSA conducts periodic security reviews and audits. Loss of FSC would eliminate PKOH's aerospace and defense revenue (~$60–120M annually). Disclosed in PKOH 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: The EPA oversees PKOH's environmental compliance, including hazardous-waste management, air-quality emissions, and water-discharge permits at manufacturing and distribution facilities. PKOH's fluid-power segment involves handling hydraulic fluids and lubricants subject to EPA regulations. PKOH maintains environmental permits for its manufacturing facilities in Ohio, Pennsylvania, and other states. No current EPA enforcement actions or violations as of Q3 2024. Disclosed in PKOH 10-K Item 1A risk factors and Item 8 environmental liabilities.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation
regulators.relationshipNote: The DOT oversees PKOH's logistics partners' compliance with hazardous-materials transportation regulations (49 CFR) for fluid-power components and industrial chemicals. PKOH's inbound and outbound freight must comply with DOT hazmat rules. PKOH's logistics partners (XPO, J.B. Hunt, DHL) maintain DOT safety ratings and hazmat certifications. No current DOT enforcement actions against PKOH or its logistics partners as of Q3 2024. Disclosed in PKOH 10-K Item 1A risk factors.
